updates.title: New Line shows the fields Title and Description with question prompts
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QA build.

steps: Open {Work-order-1} and go to its Lines tab.
Click New Line.
Without typing anything, read the label of the first field and the grey text inside it.
Read the label of the second field and the grey text inside it.
Click into the second field and type a description (for example excessive play).
Read the second field's label and what is inside the box.
Click into the first field and type a title (for example Replace tie rod). Do not pick a canned line.
Read the first field's label and what is inside the box.
Close the window without saving.
results: Step 2: the New Line window opens with the cursor already in the first field.
Step 3: the first field is labeled exactly "Title" and shows the grey prompt "What are you doing?" inside the box.
Step 4: the second field is labeled exactly "Description" and shows the grey prompt "Why are you doing it?" inside the box.
Step 6: the label still reads "Description". The prompt "Why are you doing it?" is gone and only the typed text shows.
Step 8: the label still reads "Title". The prompt "What are you doing?" is gone and only the typed text shows.

updates.title: An over-long line is shortened from the end in the report, title kept
preconditions: You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QA build.
Require Tech Story (Settings, Work Orders tab) is off.

Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open for {Customer-A} and {Asset-A} at {Location-A}, not invoiced.

{Work-order-1} has a labor line {Line-1} whose Title is exactly 16 characters (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-17) and whose Description is exactly 5,000 characters: the digits 0123456789 repeated 500 times, with no tech story.
{Work-order-1} has been completed and invoiced as invoice {Invoice-A} (for example 10234), dated {Invoice-date-A} (for example 13 Oct 2026).
steps: Open the Reports page and click Export Reports (if it is not there, open it from Administration).
Choose the Customer Invoice report.
Set the date range to cover {Invoice-date-A}.
Download the report.
Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet (for example Google Sheets: File, Import, Upload).
Find the row for {Line-1} on invoice {Invoice-A} and read its ItemDescription cell.
Click an empty cell, type =LEN( then click that ItemDescription cell, type ) and press Enter.
Click another empty cell, type =RIGHT( then click the ItemDescription cell, type ,10) and press Enter.

results: Step 6: the cell holds the title, " - ", then the start of the description; it is shorter than the full 5,019 characters (16 + 3 + 5,000).

Step 7: the number is 4000 (16 characters of title + 3 for " - " + the first 3,981 characters of the description = 4,000). Plain digits and letters take one unit each, so 4,000 characters is the 4,000 limit.
Step 8: the last ten characters are "1234567890": the end of the description was cut, and nothing trails after it (no hyphen, no space).
Step 9: the cell starts with the full title and " - 0123456789" (with the example title "ZZAUTOTEST-WW-17 - 0123456789"): the title survives whole.

quotes: S3-R7

When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.
S3-R8
The values themselves are unchanged. Nothing is trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped that is not trimmed, truncated, re-cased or escaped today, other than the shortening described in S3-R7.
Tech plan FR-011
If the joined text exceeds 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end, never mid-character, on both routes; title survives; an over-long line still syncs (S3-R7, S3-R7a, S3-E3).
SV-10132 acceptance criteria

Given a joined text longer than the QuickBooks limit, when it is sent, then it is shortened from the end, the cut does not fall inside a character, the title is intact, and the invoice syncs rather than landing in Unexported Items.

quotes: S3-R7

When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.
S3-R7a

The limit is a storage limit rather than a count of what a reader sees, so a line written with accented or non-Latin characters may be shortened more than an English line that looks the same length on screen. Two lines that look equally long can therefore be cut at different points. That is correct behavior and not a defect.
Tech plan FR-011
If the joined text exceeds 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end, never mid-character, on both routes; title survives; an over-long line still syncs (S3-R7, S3-R7a, S3-E3).

quotes: S3-E3
A description long enough to be cut still syncs. The invoice reaches QuickBooks; it does not land in Unexported Items.
S3-R7

When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.
S3-R4
The same text is used by the live QuickBooks sync and by the downloadable Customer Invoice report. The two can never show different text for the same line.
SV-10132 acceptance criteria

Given a joined text longer than the QuickBooks limit, when it is sent, then it is shortened from the end, the cut does not fall inside a character, the title is intact, and the invoice syncs rather than landing in Unexported Items.
